---
title: "Crawl"
---

`scripts/` holds the crawl, from candidates to a packaged release. Everything is
written under `scripts/scjn/`, which is gitignored: data is never committed. A
human runs the publish step.

1. **Discover.** `discover_federal_laws.py`, `discover_federal_reglamentos.py`,
   `discover_federal_lineamientos.py`, `discover_federal_tratados.py` and
   `discover_federal_estatutos.py` list
   candidates and stop: no state is written, because a new law is a human's
   decision. `scjn.discovery` holds the shared paging and rescue rules.
2. **Seed.** `seed_federal_reglamentos.py --coleccion {reglamentos,lineamientos,tratados,estatutos}`
   turns a reviewed list into `estado.json` files, idempotently.
3. **Crawl.** `fetch_scjn_legislacion.py` crawls (`--coleccion`, `--plan`, and for
   `leyes` only `--actualiza`/`--solo-fecha`/`--dof-only`/`--reintenta`);
   `recrawl_scjn_outline.py` re-crawls a whole corpus with the markers on;
   `rewrite_scjn_from_raw.py` rewrites Markdown from the kept raw answers without
   the network.
4. **Link.** Linking new `leyes` reforms to their `codNota` is `nota2md`'s
   `scripts/enlaza_scjn_legislacion.py`, in that repository. The id-keyed
   collections have no DOF linking.
5. **Verify.** `verify_scjn_outline.py`, then `measure_block_gaps.py` (see
   [Outline](outline.qmd)).
6. **Backfill the classification** (instruments crawled before the SCJN's whole
   classification was recorded). `backfill_scjn_classification.py --coleccion
   {leyes,reglamentos,lineamientos,tratados,estatutos}` asks the SCJN's search once per
   instrument and merges `categoria_ordenamiento`, `ambito`, `pais`, `estado`,
   `municipio`, `materia`, `vigencia` and `resumen` into its `estado.json`. It
   keeps only the hit whose `idOrdenamiento` equals the instrument's own, never
   ranks, is resumable (an instrument that already has `ambito` is skipped unless
   `--force`), warns about and skips a transport error and always exits 0;
   `--dry-run` writes nothing. It talks to the network (about 2,900 instruments,
   roughly 30 to 60 minutes), so a human runs it, after the crawl and before
   packaging.
7. **Package.** `empaqueta_scjn_leyes.py` and
   `empaqueta_scjn_coleccion.py --coleccion ...` build the release: tarballs,
   `indice-global.json.gz`, `SHA256SUMS.txt`, `MANIFEST.md`, `partes.json` and
   `PUBLICAR.md`.
8. **Publish.** A human reads `PUBLICAR.md` and publishes; only changed tarballs
   need `--clobber`. No script uploads anything. See [Releases](releases.qmd).

The commands a human runs to bring the classification into a published release:

```bash
python scripts/backfill_scjn_classification.py --coleccion leyes
python scripts/backfill_scjn_classification.py --coleccion reglamentos   # likewise lineamientos, tratados, estatutos
python scripts/empaqueta_scjn_leyes.py
python scripts/empaqueta_scjn_coleccion.py --coleccion reglamentos
# then publish what PUBLICAR.md says: only the index asset changed, so
gh release upload scjn-leyes indice-global.json.gz --repo legistlan/scjn --clobber
```

`scjn-estatutos` (the federal instruments the SCJN classifies `ESTATUTO`, 379 at the
audit of 13 November 2026) is crawled the same way as the other id-keyed collections, but
it is **not published yet**: its discovery, crawl and publication are still a human's to run.

The three scripts that link laws to the DOF (`discover_federal_laws.py`,
`fetch_scjn_legislacion.py`, `recrawl_scjn_outline.py`) import `dofjson` and
`nota2md` from PyPI, never the package: `uv sync --group scripts` or
`pip install dofjson nota2md` (see [Install](install.qmd)).
